pr_title: Fix locking a layer reverts changes (fix #4586)
pr_body:
fix #4586

Some comment about the approach:
This solution solves the problem and seems like a more intuitive behavior.

Anyway, I don't like the following case:
1. `lock` the layer while there is an active selection.
2. `unlock` the layer without any movement of the selection.
Result: The original selection mask will be a new mask containing any parts that were overlapped before step 1. See the following video to understand:
![Nov-19-2024 20-05-15](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d8c787e-c2d0-40f7-8fd6-d7dbdf9eddf8)
Note: this was also happening with the layer visibility state change.
I need some feedback on the approach.
pr_comments: I see that `onBeforeLayerVisibilityChange` and `onBeforeLayerEditableChange` have unused arguments (`editor` and `newState`). I left it as is, since that was the case in the existing `onBeforeLayerVisibilityChange` function. Personally I would remove them.
My first commit with the pre-commit implementation.
I'm leaving it as is despite clang-tidy's recommendations. I'm afraid of making changes and having to go back with the modifications for style/readability reasons.

issue_context.title: Locking a layer reverts changes
issue_context.body:
I have found a bug: When I lock a layer and switch to another layer, the last change may be reverted. I have tested this for the following specific steps, but it is possible that it also occurs for other types of changes.

Here are the steps to reproduce:
* Create an empty image
* Add a second layer (Layer 2)
* Select Layer 1
* B for brush tool
* Draw something
* M for marquee tool
* Ctrl-A to select all
* Arrow up to move the Layer 1 contents one pixel up
* Lock Layer 1
* Select Layer 2

Now the contents of layer one should automatically revert to their position before they were shifted up.

![2024-08-04_14h56_16](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9443a2e-7745-4a26-be7e-c549cde60c6c)

### Aseprite and System version

* Aseprite version: 1.3.7-x64, Steam
* System: Windows 10
